title: #16: an open group with a stuck member waits for its decision unless nothing needs it (D-097)
objective: An open group keeps every member and waits for the decision on a stuck member while a ticket directly depends on it or the group has another member that is neither merged nor cancelled; otherwise (nothing directly depends on it and every other member, if any, is merged or cancelled) the stuck ticket leaves the group without a group and the group goes on (pr when a merged member remains, cancelled when no member remains).
outline: ticket_controller.py: a predicate (suggested name stuck_holds(data, ident, group), or a pure function in core/chain.py so the issuer can use it too) = some ticket not cancelled lists ident in depends_on, or some other member of the group is neither merged nor cancelled. open_stays(): also True while a member with group == gid is stuck and holds. can_still_start(): a dependency that is stuck counts like a ready one when its group is open and is this group or earlier in chain.order. close_open() (runs only when nothing holds): each stuck member with group == gid leaves first (group and target None, removed from members, the event of acceptance 3), then the ready members as today, then pr / stuck / cancelled as today (a stuck ticket that was the only member leaves and its group is cancelled with 'no tickets left: group closed'). idle_lines(): the '<gid> waits for the decision on #N' line. tick() needs no change: open_has_work ignores stuck members, so a group held only by a stuck member is not busy and a run without --forever ends (project memory: a new wait must stay out of what counts as busy). Docs: ticket_controller.py docstring item 2 and the devloop/README.md paragraph that starts 'members leave it, then it becomes pr' (the groups/chain section) say what a stuck member does to its group, citing D-097; the README row of ticket_controller.py in the command table lists the new idle line. Out of scope: placing tickets that have no group (the next ticket), the stuck page's text (the one after it), repairing T's pool.

Items 1-5 in process: copy GroupFollowUnits' setUp (DEVLOOP_* popped from self.env and os.environ), group() and ctl() helpers from tests_devloop/test_groups.py into the class (do not subclass it), write tickets with self.add(N, state=..., group='g1', target='int/g1', deps=[...]) and groups with group(), then c = self.ctl(); c.advance_groups(self.snap()); read self.snap(). Items 6-7 with self.controller() / self.run_py('tickets.py', 'ready', '1') after popping DEVLOOP_TICKET, DEVLOOP_GROUP and DEVLOOP_SLOT from self.env, harness tickets added with self.add(1) and self.add(2, deps=[1]) (adoption gives #1 g1 and #2 g2, measured); the idle page's item lines are its lines that start with '#' or 'g' (as T63Acceptance.item_lines). Expected values come from D-097 and the line format in acceptance 6, never from ticket_controller.py. Before the change (measured 2026-11-24 on main with these fixtures): 1 #2 leaves and g1 becomes stuck; 2 g1 becomes pr, #3 leaves g2 and g2 is cancelled; 3 #1 stays a member; 4 #2 leaves; 5 g1 becomes stuck with members ['1'] and #1 keeps g1; 6 the lines are ['#1 stuck (decision): need the user', '#2 ready, waits for: #1 stuck', 'g1 stuck: no ticket of the group got merged'] (#2 left g2, g2 cancelled); 7 #2 leaves g2 in the first run, tickets.py ready 1 takes #1 out of g1, and #1 and #2 land in new groups g3 and g4. Implementer: item 8 (run test_group_members, test_groups, test_controller, test_issuer and test_chain once - they hold every loop case that makes a ticket stuck - and change in place only assertions about a stuck ticket's group (state, members, events, idle lines), naming each in the hand-in) and unit tests of the predicate in tests_devloop/test_groups.py between class GroupFollowUnits and class T104Acceptance, including a stuck ticket alone in its group and one beside only cancelled members (neither holds).
notes: D-097 (docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-24, the user's ruling on issue #16): 1. a group with a stuck ticket goes on to its regression without waiting only when no ticket directly depends on the stuck ticket and the group's other tickets are all done (merged); the stuck ticket then leaves the group and has no group. 2. Otherwise (a ticket directly depends on it, or the group has unfinished tickets) the group waits for the decision on it: it is not closed and no member is moved out. 3. A ticket with no group is placed by the main session and the user (ready, which group, or cancel); the controller opens no new group for it and puts it at no chain end. Reading of D-097 1 (revised 2026-11-24 after the worker's report): its two conditions are read as written. Cancelled members count as neither done nor unfinished, and a group with no other member meets 'the others are all done'. So a stuck ticket alone in its group, or beside only merged or cancelled members, that nothing directly depends on leaves; the group then goes on as close_open does today: pr when a merged member remains, cancelled when none remains (an empty group has nothing to verify). An earlier reading (a stuck ticket with no merged companion holds its group) was dropped because an open group holds the chain: one lone stuck ticket that nothing needs would stop every later group from landing. Measured on the worker's WIP branch t/134: in test_issuer's out-of-rounds case, an unrelated #2 in g2 ended merged, not landed. That goes against D-097 1's intent, and against core/chain.py holds(), where a stuck group with no merged ticket does not hold the chain. A second stuck member is an unfinished ticket, so each of them holds the group (D-097 2). The behaviour before the change was measured for acceptance 1-7 on 2026-11-24 with the loop harness (opener scratch tests: /home/user/agent-control-devloop/runs/creator/2026-11-24T133548Z-a1/repro/test_zz_repro16.py for 1-4, the revision's fixtures for 5-7). The fixtures of 5-7 were also run on the WIP branch: 6 and 7 give the expected lines and groups there; 5 does not yet, because the WIP holds a lone stuck ticket. The new idle lines of the old T63 case (item 8) are inferred. The request also wanted adopt() to move dependents into their dependency's group; D-097 3 replaces that (no automatic group at all), which is the next ticket of this hand-in. Group new-g2: the #16 tickets share ticket_controller.py and the README groups paragraph; they have no code dependency on the #14/#15 group. Out of scope: D-098 (recorded during this run: a ticket branch is rebased onto its group branch at each round start and carries only its own commits when it changes group); placing a ticket that left its group into another one with actl dag still reuses its old branch until a D-098 ticket lands.

## Issue #15: a restarted controller starts a second issuer for a running ticket
T (A at b5564f9, macOS): after a controller restart done as #11's answer recommends (SIGTERM to `ticket_controller.py --forever` only, children left running), the old issuer of #320 (pid 84547, started by the previous controller, ppid 1 after the restart, running r3-worker through a wrapper `alternate.sh -> agy.sh`) was not adopted: the new controller started a second `ticket_issuer.py --id 320` (pid 66766), which ran an r2-worker in the same worktree `t320` on `t/320`. The r2 worker saw the other run and handed in `blocked`; #320 went stuck. The orphan then began merging main into t/320 (20:15:17 local). It ignored SIGTERM (agy.sh waits for agy) and had to be SIGKILLed.
What the main session read in the code (inference, not measured):
- The controller adopts a live issuer by the ticket's `run` stamp (ticket_controller.py finish_jobs, osx.stamp_dead). A second issuer can only start after the ticket is back to ready: `_release_orphan` (stamp judged dead) or the issuer's own `release()` on a signal (ticket_issuer.py _go, Interrupted), which sets ready and round-1. The new issuer running r2 while the old one ran r3 fits the second: the old issuer got a signal, released the ticket (r3 -> round 2), and then did not exit - its interrupted_costs/stop_agents path may block on a wrapper that ignores SIGTERM, or the process went on to the merge step.
- Find out which, by reproducing with the loop harness (a fake agent command that ignores SIGTERM; stop the controller as T did; also signal the issuer). Write the measured cause in the ticket.
Wanted:
- A ticket never has two issuers at once: the issuer holds a per-ticket lock (flock on a file under the worktrees root, like gitx's worktree lock) for its whole life; a second issuer for the same id refuses at once (exit 2, one line) and touches nothing.
- An issuer that has released its ticket (interrupted) does no further work on it: no merge, no push, no pool write other than the release; it stops its agents' process trees (kill_tree, escalating to SIGKILL after a short grace when a wrapper ignores SIGTERM) and exits.
- A restarted controller adopts a live issuer (stamp alive) and does not dispatch the ticket again while that issuer (or its lock) lives.

## Issue #14: a ticket's worktree disappears during a chain fall-through after quota
T: three cases on 2026-11-24 (#369 reviewer, #351 worker, #354 reviewer): the first command of the role's chain (agy.sh) said "usage limit reached"; about 3 minutes later the next command (claude) could not start: `no command for reviewer could start (cannot start claude: not found ([Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../tabby_pool_wt/devloop/t369'))`. By then `t369` and `t369-cases` were gone and not in `git worktree list`. The ticket went stuck.
Inference (main session, not measured): the cases were the same afternoon as #15; a second issuer for the same ticket that ends (stuck) runs `Issuer.cleanup()` and removes the worktrees the first issuer still uses. Check this first; if it is not the cause, find what removed the worktree (grep every remove_worktree / prune / rmtree caller).
Wanted:
- A ticket's worktree survives a quota wait and a chain fall-through (nothing but its own issuer removes it, and only at its end).
- If the worktree is missing when the next command of a chain starts,
